summary: httpz-requests ships a Telegram-controlled remote shell as a typosquat of requests/httpx
details: The package is distributed under a name that is a short-edit variant of the popular PyPI packages `requests` and `httpx`, and its publisher metadata is left as unfilled placeholders (author `Aapka Naam <you@example.com>`, project URLs pointing at `github.com/YOUR_GITHUB_USERNAME/httpz-requests`). Its self-declared purpose is a 'Telegram bot module for remote VPS management'. All executable logic is delivered as x86_64 Linux Cython-compiled shared objects (`bot`, `cli`, `core`, `handlers`, `constants`, and a module literally named `obfuscate`) built with `CYTHON_COMPRESS_STRINGS`, so the embedded Telegram bot token, controller chat IDs, and shell command strings are not readable in the shipped artifact; no `.py` sources accompany the `.so` files. The package's `__init__.py` imports `from.bot import start_bot`, and the console entry point `httpz-requests = httpz_requests.cli:main` launches the Telegram bot. Once running, the bot receives messages from a remote operator and executes them as shell commands on the installer's host (owner allowlist visible as the `_env_owners` symbol in `cli.so`), giving the operator interactive remote code execution on any machine where the package is installed and started.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
